output.summary: KEP-1143 clarifies that the node-role.kubernetes.io/* label namespace is for end users and external consumers and must not vary Kubernetes behavior, and defines a migration for internal consumers. Status is implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Components inside Kubernetes (e.g., node-role.kubernetes.io/master) had begun depending on node-role labels to change behavior, contrary to the label's original approval, and this made self-hosting harder. The KEP restricts the label namespace to end-user and external use and sets a migration path. Per the discussion, the final remaining step was kubernetes/kubernetes#100776, which landed by August 2021, after which the issue was closed.

alternatives.option: Keep node-role labels as internal behavior switches
alternatives.why_not: The readme says this was unintentional and conflicts with the label's approved guidance, and that it limited conformant distributions from self-hosting.

evidence.quote: Clarify that the `node-role.kubernetes.io/*` label is for use only by users and external projects and may not be used to vary Kubernetes behavior.

Over time, several changes to Kubernetes core and related projects were introduced that depended on the `node-role.kubernetes.io/master` label to vary their behavior in contravention to the guidance the label was approved under.
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100776 is the only remaining action, according to the KEP.
kubernetes/kubernetes#100776 landed, shall we close then?
